entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | I am looking forward to being at the graduation ceremonies in June as a new board member. Almost all of the students will have turned 18 well before that day. With diploma in hand they can open a credit card, get married, accept thousands dollars in student loans, potentially be sentenced to prison, and enlist to serve in the military, among many other responsibilities of adulthood. It would be foolish to describe them as children one day and an adult the next. Despite this fact, a few individuals tried to ban books from our schools that include sensitive topics because they said students cannot handle it. Walking across that stage does not magically change students into an adult. Preparing them for success includes discussion of adult concepts before graduation. Pretending alcohol and drug abuse, suicide, sexual assault, racism, and other trauma don't exist is a foolish idea. It is likely some of our students have already been victims of these evils. Books can provide a safe controlled environment to expose difficult topics in the hope they can be avoided. I understand not all parents agree with me, so I support their right to opt their child out of curriculum and also prevent them from accessing the books. My understanding is none of the books were required reading to begin with. For any other instance, the teachers are already trained to make accommodations. What I do not support is the strangers preventing students from having access due to their own personal beliefs. Parents expect a well-rounded education when they enroll in FHSD, without having to supplement at home due to the objections of others. Objectively, due to the mass book challenge, the staff reviewed the list and agreed some should be removed. A few other books were located in a middle school that should be high school only. The media specialist made these decisions, and I support the outcome. This should be celebrated as policy success. The community help provide oversight and the district took action. Instead the opponents continue to insist everyone surrender to their demands without compromise. They will continue to waste district money and resources. If the students are old enough to die defending our country, they are mature of enough to discuss topics they might encounter along the way. As a board member I will grant those individuals and all other students the respect they deserve by supporting their access to age-appropriate material in accordance with all laws. I am proud to be rated GREEN by Authors Against Book Bans. Those trying to restrict knowledge are rarely on the right side of history. Vote April 7th. Books Removed: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/files/DR9TDP76E493/$file/Weeded%20List%20of%20Books.pdf Books Retained: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/files/DR9TE876F45E/$file/Books%20to%20Retain%20-%20Board%20Action.pdf | LSJf3t.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Monday, August 24th, is the first day of school for Francis Howell School District and all schools in Missouri. I want to wish a happy first day to every student, teacher, staff, administrator, and parent. My request to everyone, including the community: PATIENCE. Traffic will be everywhere. If you live near a school, be prepared for impacts to your commute. Respect all traffic and safety laws around students and busses. Based on all previous years, I already know busses will be late. Just expect the bus will not be on time any time this week, especially after school. Making sure every student makes it home safely is the priority for our drivers. If you do parent pick-up and drop-off, it won't go fast this week. Any appointments you have are at risk of being missed. Schedules can still be fixed, but there are only so many counslers. They will work as fast as they can, but it might not be at the speed you hope. Stay on top of all communications. There will be changes to something that impacts you and you could miss it. Your student(s) will be tired and stressed (as will many parents). Everyone of them will handle it different. Grant students some leeway for a few days. Especially if they fall asleep before dinner. Teachers and staff will also be tired and stressed. Give them time to respond to any issues. There is only so much time in a day and they have families, too. The weather forecast looks favorable for the start of school year. There will be a few bumps in the road, but by early September it will be routine. Smile and the world will smile with you. Reminders: Sign up for your school's PTO. Their work helps our schools in countless ways, including budget limitations. Check and see if you can help with any teacher's wishlist. Fall sports and activities are now in full swing. Come out and support students when you have time. DON'T FORGET THE FIRST DAY OF SCHOOL PHOTOS. Graduation comes faster than you think. | KuwNaj.com

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Quick Preview of Tonight’s March Board Meeting. 1-We will have elementary students leading our Pledge of Allegiance. 2-We will celebrate a Barnwell Robotics Team for winning State. 3-We will approve and sign the negotiated contract with our teachers union FHEA. 4-We will vote to approve accepting bids for different pavement and roofing projects. 5-We will listen to the results of our Workplace Culture Survey and discuss next steps to make Francis Howell better for everyone. 6-We will have a second reading and vote on Policy 6310, which largely refers to the standards we use when purchasing books for the Libraries. Note: Parents have and will continue to have the power to choose the books they want their students to be able to access. 7-We will vote on a Safe Schools Curriculum developed by FHSD that is connected to K-12 Missouri Learning Standards. 8- We will have our monthly finance report where we see the big picture financial health of the district. This report will include information for board members about the possible loss of $4 million in Year One and $54 million loss over five years if Prop RT passes. You are welcome to join us tonight or watch us online at our Francis Howell YouTube channel. | FvQTPuWXFD.com

entities.author: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Denise Leah Smith thank you for sharing your perspective and experiences. I recommend contacting the entire board via email or the superintendent. I do not have authority to make commitments via my own FB page and I want to make sure you are properly heard. That is the correct way for the board to identify any policy or procedures that would need to change. It sounds like you have serious concerns. I know the district's leadership team was struck with two horrible situations at once. They worked hard to ensure the building was safe for students and staff to return on Tuesday. Communication in these situations is very challenging. I understand that does not comfort parents, but don't interpret it as anyone in the district not caring. A majority of the current board members have students attending FHSD schools. The other directors previously did. We want all students to be as safe as our own. I cannot stress enough how seriously we take safety. Even as a board member I have little more information than the public. What we all know is that the district worked with law enforcement to make a threat assessment. Those professionals determined it was safe for students to return and I trust their judgement. Sorry for the brief answer. This is a complicated issue that will not be settled in a comments section.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | 2 Propositions. #OneHowell. On November 3, 2026, voters in the Francis Howell School District have an opportunity to consider two zero-tax-rate-increase ballot measures. Prop O (levy transfer): Allows the District to transfer funds from debt service to the operating budget. Prop H (bond issue): Authorizes the District to borrow money for facility repairs and improvements. To learn more about Prop O & H, please join us at the Administration Building (801 Corporate Center Drive) for an informational session on one of the following dates: - Tuesday, Sept. 29 at 6:30 p.m. - Monday, Oct. 12 at 6:30 p.m. - Tuesday, Oct. 27 at 6:30 p.m. You can also: - Visit the Prop O & H page: https://www.fhsdschools.org/propoh - Download the Fact Sheet: https://bit.ly/4xDh96e | J4wezPFRM.com

entities.author: Denise Leah Smith
entities.text: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board this comment is not to attack- i have seen multiple post by the board member in the past few days. I have written and erased my comments simply bc I stay out the comments. While you and possibly the others intent is not to minimize anything it may be easier to trust the intention behind all of your posts had parents of children in the district like myself who have had children had multiple serious issues handled far better over the years. When does proactive behavior become better than reactive behavior. Outside of what happened with the staff situation i have YET to see any statements released on the safety of the children regarding the targeted text threats that went out. After a hour or 2 it was deemed not a threat? Is that on a threat when it ACTUALLY becomes fatal and deadly? Imagine the fear of those parents and children? With all the school shootings we have in this country francis Howell district seems to take these threats pretty calmly and lightly. Just ask me how I know. If you'd like to know more feel free to personally message me as no one from the board even bothered to get back me when my son's school handled his threats so "well" a year ago. You want us to trust you and believe our children are safe in this district? Then have a ZERO tolerance from students to faculty. Feelings aside. We should be protecting our CHILDREN. Their teacher (most from what i have seen) do the best with what they have and what the are able to do. But this trickles from the top down and that starts with you guys. You say you have rage and grief? So do we bc we trust that we are sending our kids to a place where they are safe. And sorry when it comes to my kid I don't place blind faith in people I go by actions. So in full for some of us it's not JUST this one instance (and my kid doesnt go here but is supposed to next year) it's cumulative.

entities.text: Mindy Darrow I wish we lived in a society that was accepting of people making quick, intuitive decisions for the sake of their safety and the safety of others. However, too often we see that people are able to hide from scrutiny behind identity labels that certain political and cultural institutions have deemed to be sacrosanct and beyond question. I still remember the “Achmed the clock kid” incident from back in the Obama years, and how the teachers and school administrators made a quick decision with the safety of their students in mind and were later pilloried as “racists” and “Islamophobes”. Safety should be everyone’s right and priority, regardless of who’s feathers might get ruffled.

entities.author: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Hap Edanz I understand that politics is extremely present in our society. I am aware that many of the most vocal detractors of our schools claim to represent a specific political identity. On this issue I hope our community can step back from that, because it can only work to divide us. I see only two groups: those that support our schools and those who don't. I know from experience that our Francis Howell supporters come from the entire spectrum of political beliefs. I also know our supporters far out number those against us. Together our positive voice can drown out the negativity. That is the only way we come thru this stronger, together as a community.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | **** UPDATE: I had to miss the meeting due to a personal conflict. Hopefully this is the only time I miss. I have no updates to share, but everythjng should be on the webpage. *** Next Monday, August 31st, is the first meeting of the new school year for the Francis Howell School District Policy Committee. As the newly elected board delegate on the committee I thought I should start posting notices about the meeting. A few ground rules about my policy committee posts. First, nothing I post should be construed as the opinion of the board or indication how anyone will vote. This is for informational purposes only. Second, I am not representing any other members on the committee. There are lots of voices on the team and I am only one of them. Third, accept that this is a quick summary and I might miss something. For details, go to the official meeting notice. Forth, commenting on Facebook should not be considered a viable way to provide input. I recommend emailing the superintendent or the entire board to share any feedback about policies. Finally, remember everything is a draft update. Final wording is approved (or declined) at board meetings. On to the good stuff. The August policy committee meeting is posted to Diligent for all the public to see (Link in comments). On this month's Agenda: District Directed Changes: 1) Policy 1320 Website Accessibility - This is an update to meet legal requirements and general updates 2) Policy 0310 School Board Organization - Fix for a missing paragraph intended to already be included 3) Policy 6105 Basic Instructional Programs - Modification of reading intervention plan requirements Board Directed Changes: 1) Policy 0380 Electioneering - Update related to FHSD specific elections 2) Regulation 0380 Electioneering - Update related to FHSD specific elections 3) Policy 1420 Community Use of District Facilities - Update for high school hockey teams and also public tennis court usage 4) Regulation 1420 Community use of District Facilities - Update for high school hockey teams and also public tennis court usage 5) Regulation 1471 Public Solicitations/Advertising - Modification for what information can be posted/shared with school resources | 4CRLH.com

entities.author: Kris Newman
entities.text: One thing that I have seen and heard people say is that we have "too many people" working in admin. I have seen the numbers and I know that is NOT true! However, I wish people knew the roles that people in admin play and how they are vital to our district. Also I'd LOVE to see more FHSD alumni stories featured. We have students who have gone into some pretty incredible careers, post secondary opportunities, community impact roles, etc. I think tax payers should see the end result of a FHSD quality education. FHHS Girls Tennis Senior Night is currently planned for 10/5 at 3:30. If you can swing by the match (or any other) we'd love to have you and any board member. So grateful for our amazing courts! Thanks for serving our district!

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Followers or Francis Howell School District patrons, what do you want to see on this page? Wait, don't go straight to comments. Read the boring stuff below and then comment. First off, welcome back everyone to a new school year. Its fun to be a very tiny part of this amazing district and its annual renewal. If you are a PTO, booster, or fundraising group, you already know I want to support if I can. Always feel free to reach out and invite me. If its a school event, performance, competition, also invite me. No promises. Just like FHSD, my time & budget are limited. Back to the main topic. I am struggling on how to best use this page. When campaigning I was speaking for myself. Now on the board, that has changed. I dont speak or take action on behalf of the board. That leaves me wondering what to post. Sharing general FHSD information is one option. The district, schools, and organizational pages are already a more direct link for that, making anything I post redundant. Posting board information is another redundant possibility. The district website already has all the documents and meetings. The Board President, currently Steven Blair, shares the board agenda and meeting notices. He also summarizes each board meeting. Other than sharing his post, not much for me to add. I recommend you follow his page or any future board president. Using posts to gather feedback is limited in its benefit. It is not that I undervalue comments & feedback, but social media comments are a small sample size. The page is one data point of many. The districts existing community outreach and feedback effort is a better place to hear all voices necessary for making final decisions. Education related information could be useful. Since joining the board I now get newsletters, emails, and other general information about education. I can try to pass on anything I see that impacts our schools or community. Any post risks delving into discussions that are not board focused. Most school issues should be addressed with a teacher, principal, or superintendent, in that order. For anything critical, it is better to contact the entire board via email. Every board member is using their page differently. What do you want to see when you come here? | FSS0isDm.com

entities.author: Antonio Gutierrez
entities.text: In the end it is a lot of non-sense to justify something that is unjustifiable. There is a lot of talking points about potential damages, but then please show real data, real cases and numbers of those cases. I have been using the courts for years and I have never seen any damage. Tennis players are for the vast majority very mindful of the courts as we know the value of them. If those cases of damage / vandalism happened the district has probably tools to find the ones responsible and take the required measures. I could understand this topic if we talked about facilities with grass that would demand additional maintenance for high usage. Tennis courts are not like that. The quality of the materials, the accuracy of the project and weather are the main causes for the repair needs over time. Voters are getting what they asked for. It is funny (or sad) that people put liberals on the District Board and they get less freedom. Zero sense of community, complete disregard of taxpayer money and several paragraphs of empty content.

entities.author: Erin Ward
entities.text: I would like the board to look into the use of facilitron service that is used for reserving the school gyms. I was interested in renting out basketball gyms for practice for a club basketball team & the price on the sites says $25-$50/hr but then there are additional fees for supervisors/maintenance people to staff plus insurance & for 1 hr rental ends up costing around $600. I read the company does not charge schools to facilitate this which is great but i think it’s a loss of money coming in because who can afford that much & the rec plex only costs $60/hr, so the schools are not used & probably not generating much income from the facilities

entities.text: Honestly, as soon as things are damaged though, the school district will be blamed for not caring for resources. If we were flush with cash and there could be supervised hours I would be all for it. Wouldn’t it massively increase our liability to have all this open access?I’m empathetic to the issue as a sports parents myself, not trying to pick on tennis, but we’ve literally never had facilities available to us.I honestly view this as not having enough rec centers in the area personally. Never really occurred to me to take issue with the schools. I feel this county is very weighted towards seniors.

entities.author: No to Francis Howell Families for FHSD
entities.text: 100% outdoor facilities like tennis courts should be open for use by the public outside of school hours and events.If an extra cost ends up being associated with this it should be itemized and made known - one can always shut down facilities reactively if need be.FHN track used to be open to public use, from what I recall, for instance.It would be interesting to have an accounting of the cost to open to the public vs not frankly though, grounding people in extra costs they want might help in making it clear why underfunding the district isn’t a good thing. (Obviously if you have a budget shortfall of millions and if opening tennis courts makes matters worse …. Tennis courts should be closed before teachers are asked to suffer more)

entities.author: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: First, i want to be very clear, the locking of the courts is not related to Prop H. The bond issue was intended to be in April, but the passage of SB1002 forced the district to move it up. I tied the two together in the theme of responsible use of taxpayer funds. With regards to the reservation system, you bring up similar points others have raised. I have never used the system. I suggest reaching out to building administrators.That answer is not intended to be a sidestep. The board sets policy, the district admin is in charge of execution. Which is why I am asking the admin if there is a reasonable way the policy should be changed.

entities.author: Ronald Froman
entities.text: Before Francis Howell Central courts were locked this spring, I witnessed several weekend mornings where all eight courts were in use by tennis players, all respecting the facilities. On a weeknight evening, I witnessed high school students of both genders playing and practicing on 4 different courts and a family supervising play and practice between two grade school age kids. It is disappointing that all these varied community members are now locked out of those experiences, especially in this era when we are needing to encourage kids to be more physically active. It feels like the locked tennis courts are serving as a poster-child to promote passing PROP H, but no where do I see any explanation as to how passing PROP H will change anything in a positive manner with locked tennis courts. Lastly, could you explain how a high school student (or anyone) would practically use the tennis court "reservation system". The website instructions are ambiguous and open ended, and also seem written more for reserving a school auditorium or similar vs a 2-4 person individual play court.

entities.author: Michael Moynihan
entities.text: When I was a kid i started playing tennis again freshmen year and was at the tennis courts most days for hours at a time. I would meet family to play and call other friends from the team to meet up. I would just go if I didnt have anybody to play and hit against the wall or ask others if they minded me jumping in with them or practicing my serve by myself. i think locking them is a bad thing! My children are still pretty little but by making it harder to find places to take them could promote some familys to stay inside on tech. If your worried about vandalism get cameras. Let kids and adults play at theier own will and get exercise on the tracks meet up with friends. I do understand not opening the basketball courts seeing as thats inside the facility. Keep some of the old things that we grew up with alive.

entities.author: Julia Rose
entities.text: Tori Ross that’s terrible. Thankfully, I don’t think fighting has been an issue on our school grounds, but reckless driving in the lots while parents are picking up has been as well as “burning out” on the playground turf. St. Peter’s PD has been called out a few times by parents for the reckless driving in the parking lots. I believe there have been some vapes found left behind as well, which is a concern when you’ve got young kids using that space who will find and pick up these items at recess. I don’t want something like that to end up in my kids hands or anyone else’s. We have a fence around our playground that can be secured, but I understand that some schools don’t have that option so there’s not much they can do to keep people out

entities.text: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board Thank you and I apologize for hijacking this post. We just don’t know who to take this issue to. I know vacation station staff as well as parents like myself have had many conversations at pickup about the behavior happening on the playground while our little ones are getting picked up. Fences with locking gates were installed last year and were being used for a short while because of some of the issues occurring. It went back to open access for some reason. Us parents have just been told to call the police, but surely there are other ways to handle it. I don’t know this is an issue at all FHSD schools. Central Elementary is on the other side of our subdivision and I never see anyone there after hours. I assumed the fences and gates were installed for the purpose of keeping the area secure after hours because there were several acts of vandalism while the playground was being renovated. It looks like it’s just being used to keep the kids secure during school hours, though.

entities.author: Sarah Johnson
entities.text: Kristin Fredricks this is what I was thinking, too. Designated times for access with a district employee supervising. Yes, that will cost money, but probably less than any potential damage caused by open access without supervision. One possible consideration for funding a supervising employee might be a small increase in the fee for sports/activities. Like, we pay a marching band fee, and that fee goes toward our instructors, composers, prop budget, transportation, etc. If a student can't afford the entire fee, many activities have some level of support they can offer so no one has to miss out. A small fee to give access to facilities may be less than booking private court time or lessons, too.For residents wishing to utilize facilities, maybe they could go by a similar system--sign up for a designated open time and pay a small fee to cover maintenance and supervision. One caveat: public access may need to be at a time when students aren't present for safety reasons. Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board

entities.author: Julia Rose
entities.text: What is the district’s policy on playground use? I have kids at Fairmount and it’s open to the public after school hours. It’s a daily gathering spot for area teens who bring their mini bikes up on the turf (damaging it) and there has been vandalism to the playground equipment (carving slurs and expletives into it) as well as leaving trash behind. It’s extremely frustrating that we can’t protect it so that it stays nice for our kids that attend school there. I know people were upset when the building started locking the gates after hours, but there are plenty of local parks to take kids to to play. Once the playground is torn up, that’s what Fairmount students will be left with. Shouldn’t preserving that space for the students in that building be the priority?

entities.author: Kris Newman
entities.text: Hi Kevin! My husband and I have been part of the FHHS tennis booster board (boys and girls) since 2019. We are SO thankful for the opportunity our kids have to play and it's been super sad to see the courts closed all the time now. Court time is extremely expensive and I feel like we are doing a disservice to those who cannot afford lessons, court time, etc. We have researched public tennis courts available within a 20 minute drive of our school and the options are very limited. Our roster size is HUGE- 90 girls and about 50 boys! Imagine all of these kiddos looking for places to play! With all of this said, our booster club has invested our own money into things for the courts that we want to keep nice of course! I don't know that a free for all is the best idea but maybe certain hours or days? If anyone would be willing to have a discussion, I know our board would gladly talk about some ideas and guidelines that might help! Maybe residents have to apply for a pass or a code to play? I don't know but I want to keep our facilities looking awesome but I also want ALL kids to have the ability to work on their game!

entities.author: Abby Denningmann Kepple
entities.text: We are blessed to not only have recreation facilities at our schools, we have a fantastic parks department in St. Charles that’s continues to add and develop more spaces for the community. I have been to McNair park tennis facilities and there is almost always an available court. Lindenwood also has open courts for pickleball with certain open hours. We all pay taxes for the parks and the facilities is comparable- I don’t think this is community issue. Continuing to have a financially viable district is top of mind and should be for all residents- and should support PROP H with a YES.

entities.authorKey: name:kevin mcguire for francis howell school board
entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Being a good steward of taxpayer funds requires balancing different needs. An example are policies regarding the community's use of Francis Howell School District facilities. Per board policy all facilities are locked when not in use, but they can be rented by the community with approval. In recent weeks individuals have inquired about using school tennis courts without the reservation system. This topic is close to home for me, because I grew up using school facilities without restrictions. I fully understand the frustration from the community when gates are locked and I would prefer everyone to have the same access I enjoyed. However, facilities are a significant cost. Regardless if they are damaged during normal public usage or purposeful vandalism, the cost is still the same. Taxpayer funds would be needed for repairs. The question before the board is if we should investigate updating policies to allow easier community access. Returning to that idea of balancing needs means the answer is complicated. The cost of building, maintaining, and repairing facilities like fields and bleachers continues to go up. Unplanned costs are hard to absorb into existing budgets. Any policy change that indirectly led to waste thru avoidable repairs would be regrettable. If that happened, other capital work could be left undone. Imagine the justified outrage if a turf field or a track needed replacement, but could have been avoided. With so many facilities our district's budget is stretched. To help that, the board is asking voters to approve the Prop H bond issue on the November ballot. The bonds will fund large capital improvements around the district and touch most buildings. Approval utilizes the district's existing budget with no change to the tax levy. Yes or no your taxes are the same and is a responsible way of living within out budget. If Prop H fails, projects will have to be postponed for years. Sadly, I am already seeing opposition to Prop H online. Some in the community want to reduce funding to our schools even though FHSD has the lowest tax levy in St. Charles. Knowing that, it might be very risky to open up our facilities. I will continue investigating a responsible way to increase community access to facilities with acceptable risk to taxpayers. In the meantime I want to know your thoughts. In addition to Prop H, would you support a policy change if it had spending impacts? | 3xaByVtRX.com

entities.author: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Great questions! All of the answers are covered at recent board meetings. If you are strapped for time here are short-ish answers.With regards to bidding and contracts, the board changed district policies based on lessons learned from the past. No work can begin until total project cost is known, a huge issue with the new building. We also have new requirements for reporting to the board more often with more details. With regards to funding, here is an oversimplified answer with example numbers: Last year the state said every school should get $100 per student, but they only had budget for $96. FHSD didn't trust them and built a budget on $95. Then at the end of the school year the state said we can only give you $94, even less than expectations. This occurs AFTER the money is spent. For this year the state still thinks we should get $100, but is only committing to $93. FHSD just approved a budget using $91, but we won't know what we get until next spring. If they only give us $90, we have a deficit in our budget. With regards to past dire messaging, look at our financial reports. We have been deficit spending. The district recieved some temporary additional funding after covid. That additional revenue is gone. We are now back to reality and it is not positive. We can only deficit spend for so long.

entities.authorDisplayName: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board
entities.authorKey: name:kevin mcguire for francis howell school board
entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | At the June board meeting we approved two ballot items that require Francis Howell School District voter approval, Prop O, a debt levy transfer and Prop H, new bonds. Both items will be on the November 2026 general election ballot. Both items are needed for fiscal responsibility. These items were in work to bring to voters next year. If we lived any county other than St. Charles, we would not be rushing to get voter approval this year. However, if we don't put it on the ballot this year, we will have to wait until November 2028 due to the new law attacking schools in our county. If approved by voters, neither item will raise taxes in any way. Voting YES or NO does not raise or lower taxes for anybody. They are tax-neutral ballot items. Voting YES helps students. Voting NO harms students. Prop O: Debt Levy Transfer The property taxes residents pay are required to go in certain fund buckets. One bucket is debt (bonds). Another bucket is operations (salaries, utilities, maintenance, etc.). With voter approval we can change the percentage going into each bucket without changing the total taxes. Voting yes results in NO NEW TAXES. Prop H: Issue Bonds This is simply borrowing money to maintain and improve our buildings. Just like a homeowner, the district has roofs, HVAC, floors, lighting, plumbing, IT, and everything else needed to have a successful learning environment. The bonds are paid back with the debt levy (taxes) we already collect. Voting yes results in NO NEW TAXES. _______________________________________ Below are a list of Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ). This is my personal list and responses. It should not be construed as official Board or district communication. I will maintain and update as necessary. _________________________________________ Prop O Debt Service Levy Transfer FAQ Q0-1) What is a Debt Service Tax Levy? The portion of your property taxes that goes to the school district is actually two separate taxes. The debt service tax levy is the taxes that can only be used to pay off debt (bonds). Think of it like money that can only be used for a mortgage payment and nothing else. These taxes cannot be spent on anything else. QO-2) What is a Debt Service Tax Levy transfer? The total property tax levy for the school is the operational tax levy and the debt service tax levy combined. They are two seperate taxes approved by voters. A transfer takes a portion of the levy for debt and moves it to the levy for operations. The total combined levy remains unchanged and therefore taxes do not increase or decrease for property owners. QO-3) Why is this on the ballot for voters? The debt service levy transfer will change how taxes are spent. It will decrease how much is spent on debt payment and increase the amount spent on operations. That requires voter approval. QO-4) Is a debt service levy transfer normal? Yes. Districts use levy transfers as necessary with approval to balance levies without increasing taxes paid. It is a fiscally responsible way to utilize taxes. QO-5) If the total tax levy is not changing, why do homeowners pay more taxes than the past? The tax levy is a percentage of assessed value, not a set number. When setting property taxes, the voters set the levy (percentage), not the total number. That levy has gone down almost every year. If property owners were paying the same rate as 2015 their taxes would be 26% higher. QO-6) Will my taxes go up if this passes? We can only say the tax levy will not change and that the taxes homeowners pay will be the unaffected by this ballot measure. The district has no control over assessed value or inflation that impact the total taxes paid. If inflation is zero, taxes will not change. If home values decrease, taxes will not change. However, if there is inflation and home value increase, taxes will be subject to the Hancock amendment. That process will occur whether or not this levy transfer is approved. Whether you vote YES or NO, taxes might change. QO-7) Does reducing the debt service levy put the district at risk of debt default? No, The district has a much lower debt percentage than what is fiscally allowed for school districts. The allowed debt is based on taxes collected and the total assessed value of the district. The amount of taxes collected to pay down the debt is large enough to cover all debt payments even after this transfer. QO-8) Why is the levy transfer needed? As learned during Prop RT, the total property taxes paid has gone up over the years due to inflation and increases in home values. At the same same time to tax levy was decreased to meet the requirements of the Hancock Amendment. All of that decrease has been from the operating levy. Decreasing the operating levy and not the debt levy has changed the percentage of taxes going to operations. In 2015 87% of taxes went to operations, 13% to debt. In 2025 83% went to operations, 17% went to debt. The levy transfer will help bring those ratios closer to the past proportions. 2015: $4.349 Operations vs $0.6713 Debt 2025: $3.305 Operations vs $0.6713 Debt QO-9) Will this transfer solve the district's financial stress? No. It is estimated approval of the levy transfer will add $5 million a year to the operating budget from the debt budget. That is less than the $6 million shortfall in state funding in the 2025-2026 budget and the $1 million yearly reduction related to the senior citizen tax relief. This measure is to lessen the financial shortfalls, not solve the funding issue.. QO-10) Why not just cut spending and reduce the budget? Despite all the misinformation and flat-out lies out there, the FHSD is the most fiscally efficient large school district in St. Charles County and the entire St. Louis metro area. We have the lowest taxes of all St. Charles county and lower than all comparable districts in St. Louis County. Our tax levy has decreased for the last two decades. We have the highest student-to-admin ratio of all large districts. If FHSD operated like other districts we would have many more people working in the district office. We spend less per student than our neighboring districts. Roughly 80% of our budget is spent on staff. In spite of all that, all metrics show FHSD is one of the top performing district in the state of Missouri. Simply stated, we have nothing significant to cut that would not directly harm student achievement. QO-11) Why not cut salaries for those “high paid” administrators? The FHSD is a large organization that employs more than 2000 individuals, making it one of the largest employers in St. Charles county. Like any company of similar size and complexity, the district needs qualified and competent individuals to operate. We are competing with private industry for these individuals. Reducing salaries will impact the talent pool needed for the district to succeed. __________________________________ Prop H: Bond Measure FAQ QH-1) What are bonds? Bonds are debt that any organization issues to raise funds that are paid back over a period of time, normally 20 years. Private companies issues bonds. The government issues bonds. Having debt is normal and is considered best practices for organizations, not just school districts. QH-2) Why do school districts issue bonds? The tax revenue collect from the operations levy is spent on yearly expenses like salaries and supplies. A large portion of it is legally required to only be spent on teachers and staff. Only a very small portion is left to spend on capital expenditures. Bonds are issued to generate the large funds necessary for normal capital projects. Without bonds it would be virtually impossible to do very large capital projects. QH-3) If issuing bonds is normal, why do voters need to approve? Bonds are debt that must be legally repaid. The board is not responsible to pay back this debt. The district is not responsible for paying back this debt. Taxpayers are responsible for the debt, which requires their approval. This is voters getting a direct say in how the district operates. QH-4) Why does issuing new bonds not increase my taxes? The debt service tax levy is the portion of property taxes collected specifically to pay debt. This levy already exists and was approved by voters in the past. The amount of tax already collected is enough to pay the new bonds. Issuing new bonds will not require any increase to the tax levy. QH-5) Why do we need bonds to pay for projects instead of paying with yearly budget? A simplified explanation is comparing it to saving up to pay cash for a house. It would take time to save the money and during that time you wouldn't have a home. Taking out a mortgage gets the house now and spreads out payments to be affordable. The same logic applies to capital projects. The cost of projects are in the millions of dollars. Saving up that amount in a short time would be extremely difficult, if not impossible. It is fiscally responsible to spread that cost out over the life of a bond. QH-6) We just did new bonds in 2018 and Prop S, why are we doing it again? School district's issue bonds in regular cycles. The funds are spent and then repayment start using the debt service levy. Eight years later, the Prop S projects are complete and it is time for the next set of capital projects. QH-7) What is the total value of the bonds this time? The district is asking to issue $150 million dollars in bonds. This is based on balancing the list of needs versus fiscal responsibility of our ability to pay the debt. The master plan has more project needs than what can be done with this $150 million. To be fiscally responsible the district is asking to complete these immediate needs and come back in 5-10 years after successful execution of these projects. QH-8) What projects will be completed with the new bonds? The board recently approved the districts facilities master plan. The plan identified all projects that the district needs to complete in the next decade to maintain our buildings. From that list the district has selected the projects that need to be completed in the next 5 years. The master plan and project list on on the district website for all to review. The list includes roofs, floors, ceilings, HVAC, labs, fields, parking lots, and everything else that has a limited life from normal usage. QH-9) Why not wait until prices are firm to ask for voter approval? That would be virtually impossible. No contractor is going to supply a free estimate for a guaranteed price years in the future. It would be fiscally irresponsible for the district to sign a contract for work without the funds to pay the work. The first step is voter approval to issue the bonds. However, that does not require the district to spend the money. QH-10) Can the district guarantee all projects will be completed for the prices listed? None of these projects are on contract. The values listed are estimates based on similar projects today. The estimates include growth for inflation. However, the final cost cannot be guaranteed until projects are on contract. Nobody knows exactly what inflation will be 3-5 years from now. Wars, pandemics, tariffs, and other factors have caused significant price changes over the last 5 years. The district is subject to the same price pressures as everyone else. All estimates are based on the information we have today. QH-11) Are you asking for voter approval for spending without knowing final estimates or cost? No, we asking for voter approval to issue bonds over a number of years to pay for estimated projects. None of the projects are approved or on contract at this time. If the bonds are approved, every project will go out for bids. After final costs are known, every project will have to come to the board for approval . All of this will be done transparent to voters. Voters will see contract cost before the contracts are approved. The board can decide to deny any project or spending if it is outside of expectations. QH-12) Has the district recently changed any policies or procedures for capital spending? Yes, the district learned from the mistakes that occurred with the FHN and changed policies to prevent it from repeating. The biggest change is no construction on any project can start until the final price is set. For the FHN project the district was already on contract for millions and site work had already began when the final price was known. That cannot happen again. Also, none of the individual projects on the list are anywhere near the scope of a new building. QH-13) After all the issues with the new FHN, why should voters approve the new bonds? In my younger days I once paid for an oil change at the dealership. I was shocked at the price and learned from that experience, but I did not stop getting oil changes or maintaining my car. I did not ask for future oil changes to pay me back for that past experience. The new FHN was 1000x worse than that, but the lesson is the same. We cannot stop maintaining and improving our buildings because of mistakes in the past, no matter how big the mistake. We learn from the past and do better going forward. Using FHN as an excuse to vote NO would only harm students. | 0q8YF.com

entities.author: Duane Huggins
entities.text: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board ok, let’s look at it this way1. Verbally attacked teachers…are you referring to the teacher that was called out for the class library books inappropriate for middle schoolers?2. Documented unauthorized spending…3k was spent for a consulting firm to review a list of inappropriate books. Roumpos confirmed the payment would be paid and was later approved by the board. The district viewed the payment as “not ideal , but also not illegal. 3. Statements making elections partisan…if you’re referring to a “conservative “ moniker on a candidates profile picture, the candidates are conservative and as I suggested to a student, maybe look up the meaning of the word conservative as it’s not at all derogatory. I’ll assume the flyer called it out to associate the candidates with the vitriol of our current president. Although I haven’t seen these comments coming from the candidates, I personally believe that the core values our two political parties differ vastly, and align with party affiliation. Anyone that doesn’t admit that, is just not being honest. 4. Teacher train/conferences canceled…No district-wide cancellation of the PD calendar or major conferences appears in the 2025-2026 board minutes, calendars, or public reports. Although funds were denied for teacher traveling to other cities, it is tied to fiscal priorities and budget pressures. I had to ask Grok on that one as I was not familiar with any cancellations. Finally, your question which PAC is partisan. Are you being serious? You can’t be serious. Ted House? A lifelong democrat not partisan? Francis Howell Forward has continuously advocated for liberal candidates and ideas that have failed across the country. Name one conservative they have endorsed. Ever. Then there is MO NEA PAC, that advocates for liberal school policies, while pretending to be sole advocates of teachers. I’m actually surprised Weingarten is not in the mixNow I’ll ask you, did you even know what this hit mailer was going to say? Do you approve of the misleading vague statements? The only things I hear from your candidates is hate and division of the Howell Families candidates, and never specific plans for the betterment of the district and students. Just vague accusations and lack of context.

Anyone that doesn’t admit that, is just not being honest. 4. Teacher train/conferences canceled…No district-wide cancellation of the PD calendar or major conferences appears in the 2025-2026 board minutes, calendars, or public reports. Although funds were denied for teacher traveling to other cities, it is tied to fiscal priorities and budget pressures. I had to ask Grok on that one as I was not familiar with any cancellations. Finally, your question which PAC is partisan. Are you being serious? You can’t be serious. Ted House? A lifelong democrat not partisan? Francis Howell Forward has continuously advocated for liberal candidates and ideas that have failed across the country. Name one conservative they have endorsed. Ever. Then there is MO NEA PAC, that advocates for liberal school policies, while pretending to be sole advocates of teachers. I’m actually surprised Weingarten is not in the mixNow I’ll ask you, did you even know what this hit mailer was going to say? Do you approve of the misleading vague statements? The only things I hear from your candidates is hate and division of the Howell Families candidates, and never specific plans for the betterment of the district and students. Just vague accusations and lack of context.

entities.text: Leslie Shepley Eilers Wasteful spending takes many forms. Fiscal responsibility is sometimes about avoiding unnecessary spending, not cutting existing. For example, when the district environment drives off great teachers, recruiting their replacements uses district resources and budgets. If we can improve staff moral and ensure they are part of the district's success, that will save money in the long term.

entities.text: I have lived in the area for 20years. This school district has got horrible. My son that went though the system. He graduated in 2021. There were more aid for him. Now my daughter is a sophomore things have really change. A lot of the programs that were available for my son are not available for my daughter. From my out look this district wants the best buildings. They can not maintain them they just rebuild them. We wasted a ton of money on the new north. I still don’t understand why a leaky roof equals and whole new football stadium with bathrooms , stands, and a concession building. You can only make patches with more money. This district has to waste a ton of money! I know I will never vote on a tax increase. With all the waste I have seen.

entities.text: I feel all of this! This semester will be bittersweet with all of the “lasts” for my two seniors that have had a fantastic 13 years in FHSD with so many amazing opportunities at elementary, middle school, and high school. Thanks for the FAFSA reminder. We have it filled out, but we need to add it (and possibly the CSS?) to 3 more schools that were applied to last week! Luckily, one of our kids has decided and is 100% committed. The other is not so patiently awaiting decisions.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | America is a melting pot of people who have brought their traditions and customs with them. In my own life I have witnessed this variety in the Francis Howell Community (especially when it involves new foods!!!). Included in those customs is a diverse list of winter and end-of-year celebrations that focus on family and friends. My household celebrates Christmas, which is evident by my Clark Griswold-inspired enthusiasm for outdoor illumination. Your family may enjoy something else, like Hanukkah, Boxing Day, Kwanzaa, Yule, Bodhi Day, Pancha Ganapati, Dongzhi Festival, or something I have yet to learn about and enjoy. They all remind us that we are connected to our community, which inspires us to do good for others. So whatever you celebrate, I am wishing you are heartfelt season's greetings and happy holidays. | dDNuX8nQ.com

entities.author: Kevin McGuire For Francis Howell School Board
entities.text: Thank you for the feedback!I don't view the vision as a set list in order of priority. I think all the items are linked and affect the others. I want it all to happen. We won't be trusted by families if we are not financially sound. And we won't attract great new teachers if we are not competitive in our hiring practices. Well rounded students only come from schools with great culture. Focusing on only one goal will hinder us from reaching our potential. Also, I understand the concern of comparing success to others, but I don't believe the top districts in the state will ever regress in their goals of higher achievement. Regardless of income, district leaders should always push for the best outcome for our students.

entities.text: Our goals should, imo, compare to where we are and came from, and not where the state is.If Jefferson county suddenly had median incomes of $250k and we remained where we are - their schools would beat ours through zero fault of our own (academic outcomes are driven significantly by wealth)Therefore while retaining or improving our performance compared to ourselves is important, it really doesn’t make sense to make education a contest between geographies.Being the best is great and all, but if everyone suddenly sucked 25% more and we stayed top 5% while sucking 25% more… this would be a loss.
